title: Scale and tiny commitments
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What tiny yes do people give you?

Jose said that if you are a marketing service for a law firm and have it ranked first, you cannot use the same intelligence for a competing law firm, because it is a conflict of interest. They will want a contract that you represent only them.
He said that the same goes for hotels and restaurants, so that service business has a limit to scaling and growth, and a software business whose customers all use it does not.
Jose asked: what is the micro-commitment people make to you? He asked for the tiny commitments in conversation.
He said that the signs are phrases like: I never thought of it that way, that is really clever, this is the same problem I face. They show the person is moving closer.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the tiny commitments you hear.
Write the phrase that shows a person is moving closer.
Write the conflicts of interest in your business.
Write how you scale despite them.
Write how you will respond to a micro-commitment.

check.q: What is a limit on scaling a service business, in Jose's example?
What are signs people are moving closer?
choices: Phrases like I never thought of it that way

recap: Know your scaling limit. Notice the tiny yeses.
